observations: Three photos show a black PlayStation console wrapped in clear plastic wrap, with the PlayStation logo visible on top.
A blue DualShock controller is placed in front of the console in all photos.
The console appears to be a PS4 model due to its shape and logo, but no model number or text is visible on the device itself.
The plastic wrap is crinkled and shows signs of handling; it is not factory-sealed.
The blue controller has a standard DualShock design with analog sticks, D-pad, and face buttons, but no branding or model number is visible.
No power cord, HDMI cable, or other accessories are visible in any photo.
The background includes a black chair and a green/blue object, suggesting an indoor setting.

claims.claim: PS4 PRO Hacked with 10 latest games installed
claims.evidence: No screen or interface shown to verify hacking or installed games. The console is wrapped and not powered on.
The console is wrapped and not powered on; no display output is shown. The claim is about capability, not current state.
No power-on test or gameplay shown. The console is wrapped and not in use.

risks.proof: Screenshot or video of the console running a pirated game or custom firmware interface.

risks.proof: Screenshot of the console's game library showing 10 games, or gameplay of at least one game.

risks.proof: Video of the controller connecting to the console and responding to button presses.

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on and showing the PS4 menu.
Screenshot or video of the game library showing 10 games installed.
Video of the controller connecting and working with the console.
Clear photo of the model label on the back or side of the console.

response.reason: The console is wrapped and not powered on, so its working condition, hacking status, and game installation cannot be verified. The model is identified by type only, and critical risks like functionality and authenticity remain unproven. Proof is needed before pricing.
